content.user_title: Create Google Calendar Events with GWS
content.value_statement: Manual event entry can be slow and inconsistent. This skill creates structured Google Calendar events from clear scheduling details.
actual_capabilities: Creates an event in the primary calendar or a specified calendar.
Sets required event titles, start times, and end times.
Adds optional locations and event descriptions.
Adds one or more attendee email addresses.
Creates an optional Google Meet conference link.
Accepts RFC3339 timestamps with explicit time zone offsets.
limitations: Requires the GWS command-line tool and valid Google Workspace authentication.
Creates events only and does not update, delete, or search existing events.
Requires explicit start and end timestamps instead of natural-language dates.
Writes to Google Calendar and should run only after user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Schedule a team meeting
use_cases.description: Create a timed calendar event with attendees, a location, and an optional Google Meet link.

use_cases.title: Add customer appointments
use_cases.description: Create consistent customer appointments with clear titles, times, descriptions, and attendee addresses.

use_cases.title: Automate operational scheduling
use_cases.description: Turn approved workflow details into events on the correct calendar with explicit RFC3339 timestamps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic event
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an event titled {title} from {start_time} to {end_time}. Confirm the details before executing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has a title and exact times.

prompt_templates.title: Add event details
prompt_templates.prompt: Create {title} from {start_time} to {end_time} at {location} with this description: {description}. Confirm before executing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs a detailed internal event.

prompt_templates.title: Invite attendees
prompt_templates.prompt: Create {title} from {start_time} to {end_time} and invite {attendee_emails}. Show the final details for confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A coordinator needs a multi-attendee meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Schedule on a specific calendar
prompt_templates.prompt: Create {title} on calendar {calendar_id} from {start_time} to {end_time}, invite {attendees}, and add Google Meet. Request confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs calendar selection, attendees, and conferencing.

output_examples.input: Create Standup tomorrow from 09:00 to 09:30 using the supplied RFC3339 timestamps.
output_examples.output: Ready to create Standup from 09:00 to 09:30 on the primary calendar. Please confirm execution.

output_examples.input: Schedule Project Review with two attendees and add Google Meet.
output_examples.output: Ready to create Project Review with both attendees and a Google Meet link. Please confirm the final start and end times.

output_examples.input: Create a customer appointment on the sales calendar with a location and description.
output_examples.output: The appointment details are prepared for the sales calendar, including the location and description. Please confirm before creation.

best_practices: Use complete RFC3339 timestamps with explicit time zone offsets.
Verify the calendar, attendees, start time, and end time before execution.
Request user confirmation immediately before creating the event.
anti_patterns: Do not create events from ambiguous dates or missing time zones.
Do not invite attendees without verifying every email address.
Do not execute the write command without explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: What information is required?
faq.answer: Every event needs a summary, start timestamp, and end timestamp.

faq.question: Can it use a calendar other than the primary calendar?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the target calendar identifier with the calendar option.

faq.question: Can it invite several attendees?
faq.answer: Yes. The attendee option can be supplied multiple times with verified email addresses.

faq.question: Can it create a Google Meet link?
faq.answer: Yes. Enable the Meet option when creating the event.

faq.question: Which time format should I use?
faq.answer: Use RFC3339 timestamps, preferably with an explicit time zone offset.

faq.question: Does it require confirmation?
faq.answer: Yes. Event creation changes Google Calendar, so the skill directs the agent to confirm before execution.
